desc:
An edit is one of: inserting a single character anywhere, deleting a single character, or replacing a single character by a different one.

Given strings s and t, return true if t can be obtained from s with exactly one edit, otherwise false. Identical strings need zero edits, so for them the answer is false.

For example, "pale" and "ple" give true (delete a); "pale" and "bale" give true (replace); "pale" and "pale" give false; "pale" and "bake" give false (two replacements).
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase letters and digits
hints: The general edit distance needs a quadratic table. Here you only need to know whether it is exactly 1, which restricts the lengths a lot.
If the lengths differ by more than one, the answer is false. Otherwise find the first position where the strings differ, scanning from the left.

At the first difference: if the lengths are equal, the rests after that position must be equal (replace); if one string is longer by one, the longer string must equal the shorter one when its differing character is skipped (insert/delete). If there is no difference at all, the answer is true only when the lengths differ by one.
editorial: Let s be the shorter (or equal length) string after a possible swap. If len(t) - len(s) > 1, return false. Find the first index i where the strings differ. If none exists inside the shorter string, the strings are equal up to len(s), so one edit is possible exactly when t has one extra character at the end.

Otherwise there is a difference at i. For equal lengths, a single replacement fixes it only if s[i+1:] == t[i+1:]. For lengths differing by one, the extra character must be t[i], so we need s[i:] == t[i+1:]. Everything is one scan plus one comparison of suffixes: O(n) time. Greedy matching of the common prefix is safe because the first difference is where the single edit has to happen.
